summary:
One proven defect, in #1137's on-behalf-of confirmation lane: clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for admits a client the human entrance refuses. Everything else I attacked held. Driven on clara_l01 (127.0.0.1:55741) inside transactions that were rolled back: with the SAME tenancy, the SAME author and the SAME arguments, the human door answers CLR10 'client is not active -- no new accounting plan' {"reason":"client_inactive"} on both non-active statuses the estate admits (archived, onboarding) while the OBO twin SUCCEEDS and writes an active recurring_journal plan. The human lane gets that wall from clara.create_accounting_plan; the OBO lane takes clara._tenancy_plan_core instead, which is a copy of clara._obo_plan_core and, like it, carries no client-status check -- but the door §I names as its line-for-line precedent, clara.create_prepayment_schedule_for (0307/#915), carries the guard itself, at exactly the position where the new twin stops, and packages/db/tests/prepayment-schedule-obo.test.mjs:374-377 drives a dedicated cell for it on BOTH entrances. That makes this an acceptance-criterion failure ('the same refusals as the human doors'), a false sentence in the migration header (§I: 'they add no rule the human door does not have') and a false claim in the two reports ('p1137.obo.refusals_match' is said to prove the refusals match). Bounded blast radius: clara._plan_admit_occurrence and clara.wake_due_plan_occurrences both refuse a non-active client, so nothing posts -- the damage is the divergence itself plus the rows written (plan, revision, contract_plan_confirmations, two audit rows) and the rent_plan_already_confirmed / payable_account_in_use walls those rows then hold against the client's later re-activation.

WHAT I COULD NOT BREAK, each driven rather than read: the tenant wall on all eight new doors (another firm's real id and an invented id answer the same sentence, on the model lane and on the human door); the ACL role by role (all ten cores 42501 from every application role, the two _for twins clara_runtime only, the six wake reads clara_agent_ro only, measured straight off pg_proc.proacl); the rank floor (clara.wake_context re-checks role_rank(m.role) >= role_rank('bookkeeper') against a LIVE active membership on every use, so a standing credential dies on demotion as well as on withdrawal); a two-session race -- two real clara_runtime connections confirming ONE tenancy at once under different op keys gave one success, one CLR10 rent_plan_already_confirmed and exactly one live plan, because the client rung 203005004 sits above the already-running read; idempotency under replay with a different payload (clara._reserve_op raises CLR10 'op_key reused with different args'); a null p_client on the two client-scoped reads (CLR11, no firm-wide leak); the splice anchors (§0 derives the pre-image forward and refuses unless the sha matches the embedded body, so a zero-match anchor aborts the apply -- and the queue core's blanket 'c.firm' -> 'p_firm' substitution is clean: 23 p_firm, 0 p_firm_id, 0 c.firm left); and the four neighbour guards, which are MOVE-gated and pin BOTH halves rather than being weakened -- I re-measured T.4's new row-lock regex and confirmed its roster's only body carrying 'for update' at all is the revision core, so nothing checked before is skipped now.

Gates I re-ran rather than took on trust: the two new batteries with the full 130-flag gate chain 30/30; operation-census + rig-isolation 33 tests / 32 pass / 1 skip (T19 poison-role, needs CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET); eight neighbour batteries that read a recut body or a moved guard 139/139 (which is also what proves the new `via` audit stamp breaks nothing); FREEZE_BASE_REF=061a6992b node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs OK 347/60/3 and git diff 061a6992b..HEAD -- frozen-workflows.json empty; CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true FREEZE_BASE_REF=061a6992b pnpm lint exit 0. Note for the integrator: my probes ran through the rig fixtures, so they left ordinary test rows on clara_l01 (a world, three fresh clients, their tenancies, and ONE committed rent plan from the race probe on its own fresh client); both probe files were deleted and the worktree is clean.

findings.title: clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for confirms a rent plan for a NON-ACTIVE client that the human door refuses with client_inactive
findings.evidence:
DRIVEN on clara_l01 (PGPORT=55741) inside transactions that were rolled back, through a real clara_runtime connection with no request.jwt.claims (the shape pools().withRuntime gives an act tool) and, for the control, a real clara_authenticated connection as the same bookkeeper. Scene: a client of firm A with the 6100/2050/1120/1010 chart, MPERS recorded through clara.capture_knowledge, a tenancy filed and driven end to end through #948's own contract-facts lane, its four readable terms recorded through clara.record_contract_terms. Then clara.clients.status was moved to each of the two non-active values clients_status_check_0017 admits and BOTH entrances were called with identical arguments:
  [archived]   HUMAN: CLR10 client is not active -- no new accounting plan {"reason":"client_inactive"}
  [archived]   OBO  : SUCCEEDED plan=d38c7062-d566-4f2b-baf3-7ab7ff228afe
  [onboarding] HUMAN: CLR10 client is not active -- no new accounting plan {"reason":"client_inactive"}
  [onboarding] OBO  : SUCCEEDED plan=d74f89b7-515f-48eb-873e-d3319835265f
  [active]     HUMAN: SUCCEEDED   OBO: SUCCEEDED   (the control)
WHY: the human lane's plan step is clara.create_accounting_plan, whose body carries `select c.firm_id, c.status into v_client_firm, v_client_status ... if v_client_status <> 'active' then raise exception 'client is not active -- no new accounting plan' using errcode='CLR10', detail='{"reason":"client_inactive"}'`. The OBO lane's plan step is the NEW clara._tenancy_plan_core (0353 §F), which begins at 'THE AUTHORITY SHAPE, verbatim from clara.create_accounting_plan' and never reads clara.clients at all; clara._confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_core reads the client only for its firm_id, and clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for reads it only for its firm_id too. MEASURED on the live catalog: prosrc ~ 'client_inactive' is TRUE for create_prepayment_schedule_for and create_revenue_recognition_schedule_for, FALSE for confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for, _confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_core, _confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_revision_core and _prepayment_schedule_core. The precedent §I names line for line -- clara.create_prepayment_schedule_for (0307, #915) -- puts the guard in the TWIN, immediately after its insufficient_role check (lines 38-41 of its body), precisely because _obo_plan_core does not carry it; and packages/db/tests/prepayment-schedule-obo.test.mjs:372-377 drives it on both entrances ('`archived` is the estate's own non-active status (`clients_status_check_0017` admits active | archived | onboarding); the door's token for any of them is `client_inactive`'). No cell in this lane covers it: grep -c client_inactive on tests/tenancy-agent-twins.test.mjs and tests/agent-read-twins-payroll-agreement.test.mjs is 0/0, and reports/waveS-lane08-ticket1137.md lists p1137.obo.refusals_match's seven tokens, none of which is this one. CONSEQUENCE, bounded but real: nothing posts (clara._plan_admit_occurrence re-reads clara.clients.status and clara.wake_due_plan_occurrences filters `cl.status = 'active'`), but the OBO lane writes an accounting_plans row, a revision, a contract_plan_confirmations row and two audit rows for a client the web surface refuses -- and those rows then hold the rent_plan_already_confirmed and payable_account_in_use walls against the client when it IS activated, so the legitimate confirmation a person makes later is refused. `onboarding` is the live case: 230 clients on this rig carry it, and it is exactly the state a tenancy gets filed in during setup.
findings.required_fix: Add the client-status wall to the OBO entrance, in 0307's own shape and position: in clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for (and, for symmetry with the precedent, clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_revision_for), read `cl.status` in the same `select ... from clara.clients` that already resolves v_firm and, after the insufficient_role check, `if v_client_status <> 'active' then raise exception 'client is not active -- no new accounting plan' using errcode='CLR10', detail='{"reason":"client_inactive"}'`. Prefer that over putting it in clara._tenancy_plan_core, because the human lane's own message comes from create_accounting_plan and the twin must answer it word for word. Then: (1) extend p1137.obo.refusals_match to an eighth token driven on BOTH entrances over `archived` and `onboarding`, in prepayment-schedule-obo.test.mjs:372-377's shape (setClientStatus already exists in tests/prepayment-schedule-fixtures.mjs); (2) add the `CLR10 client_inactive` row to the successor contract's refusal mapping for confirm_tenancy_rent_plan in reports/waveS-lane08-ticket1137.md, whose table today claims 'every token below is answered IDENTICALLY by the human door'; (3) correct 0353 §I's sentence 'they add no rule the human door does not have' to say which rules the CORE does not carry and where they are applied. The migration is unmerged, so this is a `CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO=0353_tenancy_agent_twins_obo_confirmations` round (packages/db/README.md, 'Redo (#957)'), not a new number -- and the redo must re-drive BOTH branches of the bimodal prestate, since only the REDO branch runs by itself.

findings.title: clara._tenancy_plan_core is a third snapshot of the plan-creation body, and it is ALREADY behind the original it was copied from
findings.evidence: 0353 §F adds clara._tenancy_plan_core as clara._obo_plan_core's body with the kind fixed to 'recurring_journal' and the via fixed to this entrance; `diff` of the two live bodies is 11 hunks, all of them the kind/via specialisation plus comment text. The lane names the duplication honestly (migration header, `comment on function`, README § 0353, follow-up 1). What the report does NOT say is that the snapshot has already drifted from the body it claims to be 'verbatim from clara.create_accounting_plan': ADV-L08-01 is that drift, live today. It will drift again inside this same wave -- reports/waveS-lane01-ticket1051.md recuts clara.create_accounting_plan from a7c108d5dd4febbae9f98a87b42b69468aec31f1731336b2185c8e91b1b0951c to 544cd88ecaa5b5237969aff36b1bd0d8a5cdf41aacea234e6415d3df54b523ea and #1080 recuts clara._authority_ref_refusal after it, and clara._confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_core's HUMAN branch calls clara.create_accounting_plan by name (so it picks those up) while its OBO branch calls the copy (so it does not). The signature is unchanged in #1051 (same 14 named arguments), so nothing breaks at apply time -- the two entrances simply answer differently, silently, which is the whole failure mode of ADV-L08-01.
findings.required_fix: Keep the lane's follow-up 1 (fold recurring_journal into clara._obo_plan_core's closed kind set and make clara._tenancy_plan_core a two-line caller, AFTER #1051 and #1080 land) and raise it to a ticket the integrator schedules rather than a line in a report. Until it lands, the standing guard is a CELL rather than a comment: extend p1137.obo.refusals_match (or a new structural cell) so that every refusal clara.create_accounting_plan raises is driven through BOTH entrances of clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan on one scene, so the next divergence is a red rather than a review finding.

findings.title: the confirmation op-key request hash omits the named author, so a replayed key under a DIFFERENT bookkeeper returns the first one's receipt
findings.evidence: clara._confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_core hashes jsonb_build_object('client', p_client, 'document', p_document, 'rent_account', p_rent_account, 'payable_account', p_payable_account, 'judgement', v_judgement) -- p_actor is not in it, and the reservation is taken with c.firm and the human verb. The payload guard itself works: clara._reserve_op raises CLR10 'op_key reused with different args' on any change to those five, which I re-read off the live body. But a second call under the same key with the same five arguments and a DIFFERENT p_author returns the FIRST author's stored receipt, so the tool would report a confirmation as the second person's while clara.contract_plan_confirmations.confirmed_by and both audit rows name the first. This is deliberate -- §I calls it 'ONE op-key namespace' and p1137.obo.one_op_key_namespace drives the human/OBO convergence it is there for -- and it matches 0307, whose core hashes the caller's own arguments only. The reachability is narrow: the successor contract's key is stableOpKey(ctx.taskId, CONFIRM_TENANCY_RENT_PLAN_TOOL, input), so two authors would have to share one task id. Reported because the lens asks for replay-with-a-different-payload and this is the one edge the guard does not cover.
findings.required_fix: No code change needed if the ruling stands. Say it out loud where a cut will read it: add one line to the successor contract for confirm_tenancy_rent_plan in reports/waveS-lane08-ticket1137.md noting that the author is outside the reservation hash, so the chat lane's op key must never be derived from anything that can outlive the initiating person (ctx.taskId does not, which is why the contract's choice is safe).

findings.title: the authority_lost arm distinguishes another firm's client for a caller holding a DEACTIVATED member's id
findings.evidence: clara.confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_for resolves the client's firm first, then the author's membership OF THAT FIRM: no membership row at all answers CLR11 'client is not in your firm' (identical to an unknown client id -- that pair is walled, and the lane drives it), but a membership row with status <> 'active' answers CLR04 {"reason":"authority_lost"}. So a caller on clara_runtime that knows one DEACTIVATED member of firm F can tell 'this client id belongs to F' (CLR04) from 'it does not, or does not exist' (CLR11). 0353's own §I header acknowledges the asymmetry and justifies it ('they already knew the client exists'), which is 0307's ruling too, and the caller here is the runtime role, which reaches the data anyway -- so this is not a widening. It is recorded because the migration header states the stronger claim that the pair 'cannot enumerate another firm's clients', which is true of the non-member arm it is written about and not of the deactivated one.
findings.required_fix: None required. If the integrator wants the header to be literally true, narrow its sentence to the arm it describes (a NON-MEMBER author and an unknown client are indistinguishable) rather than claiming the whole ladder is oracle-free.

findings.title: p_lane is unvalidated in both confirmation cores and no cell can reach the fail-closed path
findings.evidence: clara._confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_core and clara._confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_revision_core take p_lane text and test only `if p_lane = 'obo'` for the plan step and `case p_lane when 'obo' then ... else ...` for the audit `via`. An unknown lane therefore takes the clara.create_accounting_plan path and fails closed with CLR04 'no authenticated actor' on a runtime connection -- but it also writes the audit row with the HUMAN verb, and nothing asserts either. The lane reports this itself under 'Anything unverified' and the honest reason: both cores are ungranted (pg_proc.proacl = clara_fn_owner=X/clara_fn_owner, measured) and both callers pass a literal, so no cell can drive it.
findings.required_fix: Optional, and cheap if taken with ADV-L08-01's redo: open both cores with `if p_lane is null or p_lane not in ('human','obo') then raise exception ... using errcode='CLR10', detail='{"reason":"unknown_lane"}'; end if;` -- the same closed-set line clara._obo_plan_core already carries for its kind, with the same justification in its comment ('unreachable from either caller; a later lane that widens the set finds this line instead of a silent branch').
